title: Three Evenings and One Short Letter
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事·情绪与心理）　|　核心词汇：pleasure　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pleasure 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1981 the counsellor ① gave the pleasure that no listener in the garden would have recorded, and he said the giving was the whole of the evening. The ② pleasure, meaning the joy itself and not the letter, ran three evenings and stayed unrecorded in the book; pleasure, he said, is the only thing in a garden that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ bit of pleasure in that garden had the same short letter beside it, and the ④ pleasure at the far bench, meaning the secret they kept for the children to tell and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Pleasure, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the counsellor said the recording is the part that fills three evenings.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the pleasure was the whole of the matter, meaning the grace and not the joy. The ⑥ pleasure, meaning the grace and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; pleasure, he said, is either something you give or the only word that means both joy and a grace. He said the grace is the part they remember.

By 1986 the ⑦ pleasure had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the short letter. The ⑧ pleasure of the whole thing, the counsellor wrote in June, was one garden and three evenings of recording; pleasure, he said, is either the secret at the far bench or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ pleasure I remember is the pleasure recorded in the journal, which closed in 1988 and is still recorded as the quietest in the garden. ⑩ Pleasure, my mother said in 1990, is the only thing that improves by being recorded; all pleasure, she said, is a grace that has agreed to look like joy. She said the grace was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 愉快；乐事（指小园里每一分旁边的那一分）
B. n. 愉快；乐事（指那份愉快本身，与薄薄的信相对）
C. 固定搭配：give the pleasure 带来这一份愉快
D. n. 愉快；乐事（指留给孩子们说出的那一个）
E. n. 愉快之事（抽象总称，指一处小园的愉快之事）
F. n. 愉快；乐事（指心记里写到、被记载的那一份）
G. n. 愉快、情致（指一件事里人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 情致（抽象总称，指人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: gave the pleasure that no listener in the garden would have recorded
The pleasure, meaning the joy itself and not the letter
Every bit of pleasure in that garden
the pleasure at the far bench
the pleasure was the whole of the matter
the pleasure had become a line in a journal
The pleasure of the whole thing

answers.why: give the pleasure 意为“带来这一份愉快”，1981 年那位谈心人把小园里没有一位倾听者肯记载的一份愉快做了一遍。
pleasure 意为“愉快；乐事”，指那份愉快本身而不是薄薄的信，它经过了三个黄昏而在簿子上没有被记载。
pleasure 意为“愉快；乐事”，指小园里每一分旁边的那一分，每一分旁边都有同一封薄薄的信。
pleasure 意为“愉快；乐事”，指最远那张长椅的留给孩子们说出的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
pleasure 意为“愉快、情致”，指一件事里人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份情致就是那件事的全部。
pleasure 意为“情致”，指人人都叹却无人提起的那样东西而不是那份愉快，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
pleasure 意为“愉快；乐事”，指心记里写到、被记载的那一份，到 1986 年这一份成了心记里的一行。
pleasure 意为“愉快之事”，谈心人六月写道，整件事的愉快之事是一处小园和三个黄昏的记载。
pleasure 意为“愉快；乐事”，我记得的是心记里记载过的那一份，1988 年说尽了，至今仍被说成小园里最安静的一份。
pleasure 为抽象总称，母亲 1990 年说，愉快是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的愉快。
